title: STEP import: a closed, gap-free solid wound inward imports inside out (signed volume < 0), nothing says so

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens: a STEP solid whose faces are all wound inward (consistently, so no face disagrees with a neighbour) imports with a negative signed volume. Nothing flips it and nothing says so. Seen with the local older test part `step-block-371.step` (20 facets, V = -102000 mm^3) on upstream main and on the #1576 branch alike, found in the review of PR #1576 (issue #1573). A synthetic stand-in reproduces it: `testdata/models/box.step` with every `same_sense` (FACE_SURFACE and FACE_BOUND) inverted imports with V = -1, `notes = []`.

Why #1576 leaves it: its rule flips faces only where neighbours disagree, so a consistently inverted shell is untouched. Deciding "outward" when nothing flipped is wrong for an open or lone-face shell (a curved open face's centroid volume has no meaning), so it needs a guard: closed, gap-free (the seams judge already knows) and every shared edge opposite.

What a wrong winding can do, as far as traced:
- `crates/app/src/pick/winding.rs` already refuses face picks on a wound-inward body by name, so alignment to it is refused, not wrong.
- The solid law (`crates/sim/src/verify/solid.rs`) reads the mesh by ray parity, which does not depend on winding, so the gouge check is not fooled on this evidence.
- NOT traced: generators or checks that read facet normals directly (3D finishing, pocket3d offsets, tool-side). Whoever works this should grep them and test one op on an inverted box; if any gouges or cuts the wrong side, raise to P1.

Rating: P3 (wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround: re-export or import an STL; the picks refuse). By the AGENTS.md safety floor the fix touches geometry, so effort:high.

Done means: a closed, gap-free STEP shell with every shared edge opposite and a negative signed volume is flipped outward at import and says so in the import notes (the `Graded`/MCP `notes` and status line); an open or lone-face shell is left alone; pinning tests for the inverted box and for the lone-curved-face case; the unchecked normal-reading ops listed above are checked against an inverted box and the result is commented here.

Part of / refs: #1573 (closed-shell watertight), found in the review of PR #1576.
